I graduated from college with a degree in Women's Studies (now it's called Feminist Studies) in 1995. I took a lot of classes where it seemed that the objective of the class was to purposefully push your buttons so that you could explore where your discomfort was coming from. At the same time, I was selling flowers on the street corner in a largely Hispanic neighborhood, so it was strange to see the difference between the culture as described by a feminist writer versus these individuals coming by every day to buy flowers for the cemetery or these men buying flowers for their partners. These two worlds did not seem like the same place, in my opinion, and that experience kept me grounded in reality, in a world of real people.

One feminist writer noted that the danger was in ranking oppressions. That always stuck with me. I think a lot of this stifling environment that the original poster writes about might partly be caused by the arms race of ranking oppression.
